full_judgment:
11. Admittedly, the suit tanks originally belonged to the emperor of India as the superior landlord. There are two tanks in the suit land, during B.A. operation, the two tanks were recorded in the name of the then Government of East Pakistan in Khash Khatian No. 1, but during R.S. operation those two tanks measuring an area of about 12.12 acres were recorded in the names the defendants. It is the consistent case of the plaintiff that the villagers had been possessing and using both the suit tanks for their own welfare for the last 70 years. The plaintiff also claimed that the defendants started creating obstacle to the local people in possessing the using the suit tanks. 

 12. Having gone through the Judgment of the Courts below including the High Court Division, we find that much importance was given to the judgment passed in the special Appeal No. 239 of 1962 under section 53 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Let us now consider about the said judgment. Admittedly the PRR was recorded in the name of the ex-landlord in respect of Plot Nos. 56 and 62 of Khatian No. 1/27 of Mouza-Dakurail, Police Station Kaliakoir. Against the said entry made in the PRR, Daliluddin Ahmed filed objection case No. 3053 for recording the land in his name alleging that he had taken pattan of those two tanks from the landlord. The objection case was allowed by the objection officer. Against that order of objection officer, or the Government, one Amiruddin filed an Appeal No. 1614 under section 19(2) of the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act on behalf of the villagers of Dakurail and Dhol Samudra Kutamani. The appellate officer allowed the appeal under section 19(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act but ordered that those two tanks be recorded "in the name of the Government with note in remark column-23 that those tanks would be useable by the public. After that, Daliluddn Ahmmed filed Special appeal No. 239 of 1962 under section 53 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The learned Special Judge allowed the appeal on technical ground that neither the Government nor outgoing landlord filed any appeal under Section 19(2) of the State Acquisition and tenancy Act. But one third - person namely, Amiruddin on behalf of the villagers filed appeal under section 19(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Therefore, the learned Special Judge held that the appeal filed under Section 19(2) of the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act by Amiruddin on behalf of the villagers was incompetent. As such, the learned special Judge allowed the appeal under section 53 of the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act filed by Daliluddin Ahmmed and the judgment and order passed in Appeal No. 1615 under Section 19(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was set aside as not maintainable and restored the order of objection officer who recorded the Khatian in the name of Daliluddin Ahmmed. 

 15. As regards possession, all the courts below found possession of the defendants in the suit land because of preparation of Khatian in their names and also for payment of rent by them. The Government only examined one witness, P.W. 1 namely. Wali Ahmed, Tahsildar of Fathepur Union Land office but none of the villagers was examined although the plaintiff filed the suit on the assertion that the villagers of two villages have been possessing and using the disputed two tanks for their welfare for the last 70 years, Even on behalf of the villagers one Amiruddin filed Appeal No. 1615 under 19(2) of the State acquisition and Tenancy Act and accordingly, the khatian was prepared in the name of the Government in khash Khatian No. 1 with a noting in remark column -23 that those tanks would be useable by the public, The judgment delivered in Appeal No. 1615, was, however, set aside in Special Appeal No. 239 of 1962.
